description: #3927, #5371 — BRANCH differential over `list_pages_with_metadata`'s six-arm `PageSort` keyset (`keyset_for`, `src-tauri/src/commands/pages/metadata.rs`). Every step queries the SAME three seed pages and the six arms return the six permutations of them, so each step falsifies the other five: a keyset arm wired to the wrong sort mode reddens instead of reordering invisibly. All six steps are `ordered` — a set comparison over a SORT arm proves nothing. Titles Charlie/Alpha/Bravo (alphabetical), seed ids S1<S2<S3 (created is id DESC), descendant counts 1/0/2 (most-content), inbound links 2/1/0 (most-linked), page-wide last edits S1 newest then S3 (recently-modified), and opens of S1 then S2 (last-opened). Every tie a clock could produce falls the way the expected order already reads: two edits or two opens in one millisecond are broken by the arm's id tiebreaker in the same direction. The links arrive via `edit_block` rather than the seed insert: the seed bypasses the materializer, so only an op-driven content write populates `block_links`. The opens run through `record_page_open` itself, which appends no op; `page_opens` is device-local and outside the snapshot, so the `last-opened` step is what observes it. The two `pages_last_edited_*` steps then filter the same edits by `LastEdited`, which reads the sort's page-wide `pages_cache.last_edited_ms`: no op touched a page block, so a page-only key would answer Rolling with nothing and OlderThan with all three.
name: query_pages_metadata_sorts

ops.comment: S5 and S6 are S3's children: their edits move S3 up `recently-modified` and link S1 (twice) and S2 (once).
Last edit, on S1's only child: S1 leads `recently-modified`. A page-only key would see no op on any page block and answer S1, S2, S3.
Opened after S1, so it leads `last-opened`; two opens in one millisecond tie, and the `b.id DESC` tiebreaker puts S2 first either way.
ops.name: open_alpha

ops.comment: S4 is a content block, not a page: nothing is stamped.
ops.name: open_refuses_a_content_block

queries.comment: PageSort::Alphabetical -> StringAsc on pages_cache.title_sort_key (NFKD, marks stripped, lowercased): Alpha, Bravo, Charlie.
queries.name: pages_sorted_alphabetical

queries.comment: PageSort::Created -> IdDesc (`b.id DESC`): seed-label order reversed.
queries.name: pages_sorted_created

queries.comment: PageSort::LastOpened -> I64Desc on COALESCE(page_opens.opened_ms, -1), ties `b.id DESC`: S2 (opened last), S1, then the never-opened S3.
queries.name: pages_sorted_last_opened

queries.comment: PageSort::MostContent -> I64Desc on COALESCE(pc.child_block_count, 0): 2 (S3) / 1 (S1) / 0 (S2). An ASC keyset would exactly reverse it.
queries.name: pages_sorted_most_content

queries.comment: PageSort::MostLinked -> I64Desc on COALESCE(pc.inbound_link_count, 0): S1 is linked from S5 and S6, S2 from S6, S3 never.
queries.name: pages_sorted_most_linked

queries.comment: PageSort::RecentlyModified -> I64Desc on pages_cache.last_edited_ms, the newest op on the page OR ANY OF ITS BLOCKS: S1 (its child's edit came last), S3 (its children's edits), then S2, which no op touched and whose seed-label id carries no creation time.
queries.name: pages_sorted_recently_modified

queries.comment: LastEdited Rolling{7} reads the page-wide pages_cache.last_edited_ms: S1 and S3, edited only through their children just now, pass; S2, which no op touched, does not.
queries.name: pages_last_edited_rolling_counts_child_edits

queries.comment: LastEdited OlderThan{7}, the inverse: only S2, whose seed-label id reads as the epoch.
queries.name: pages_last_edited_older_than_counts_child_edits
